## Uncovering AI

### Key Highlights
- ChatGPT has introduced an "App Store" feature, allowing for real integration and "plug-and-play" functionality with various tools and services.
- A new image model, Qwen-Image-Layered, can automatically dissect and layer any flat image.
- Meta's SAM 3D enables users to turn 2D photos into 3D printable objects.
- Google's NotebookLM has been updated with new features, including integration with other Google apps like Sheets and Slides.

### Detailed Points
- **ChatGPT's "App Store"**: This feature allows users to connect their Notion, Airtable, or Spotify accounts directly within ChatGPT, enabling native tooling and universal access. Developers can now submit their own apps, which is expected to lead to a significant increase in utility.
- **Qwen-Image-Layered**: This model can take any image and automatically separate it into independent layers, similar to how music stems work. It has potential applications in graphic design, studying compositions, and more.
- **Meta SAM 3D**: This tool can turn 2D photos into 3D models that can be printed. It works by having the user upload an image, select the object they want to extract, and then generate a 3D model that can be downloaded as a .GLB file and converted to .STL for printing.
- **Google NotebookLM Updates**: NotebookLM now integrates directly with Gemini, allowing users to link their notebooks and combine deep context with general reasoning. It also enables the conversion of research data into organized Google Sheets and can generate multimedia outputs like slide decks or audio summaries.

## Hello, World!

### Key Highlights
- LinkedIn merged its identity midtier and data services to reduce latency and operational overhead by eliminating unnecessary network hops.
- The merger resulted in a ~10% latency improvement, significant memory savings, and a major reduction in annual cost-to-serve.
- LinkedIn used a service-oriented architecture, with each service encapsulating a domain, exposing a clean API, and evolving independently.
- The company followed a four-step implementation strategy to merge the services, including merging without a full rewrite, gradual rollout using controlled experiments, decommissioning the data service, and cleaning up technical debt.

### Detailed Points
- LinkedIn's identity services handle hundreds of thousands of requests per second, making even small architectural decisions crucial to avoid significant downstream effects.
- The identity midtier and data services were initially separate, with the midtier containing most of the business logic and the data service providing CRUD operations.
- However, as traffic increased, the data service added limited value, and its operational overhead became significant, leading to the decision to merge the services.
- The merger involved embedding the data service's REST API as a local library inside the midtier, allowing it to interact directly with Espresso, LinkedIn's distributed data store.
- LinkedIn used its internal experimentation framework, T-REX, to roll out the changes gradually, monitoring latency and error metrics closely.
- The merger resulted in significant improvements, including a 14% improvement in p50 latency, 6.9% improvement in p90 latency, and 9.6% improvement in p99 latency.
- The company also saw a 28.6% reduction in memory allocation, leading to fewer GC pauses, better CPU efficiency, and lower infrastructure requirements.
- The cost-to-serve reduction was substantial, with 12,000+ CPU cores and 13,000+ GB of memory freed, resulting in significant annual cost savings.

## TAAFT - There's An AI For That

### Key Highlights
- OpenAI employees earn an average of $1.5 million in salary, bonuses, and stock options.
- Perplexity CEO warns that on-device AI could make data center investments obsolete.
- Plaud launches a new AI pin and desktop notetaker, capturing 20 hours of audio with 64GB storage.
- Google introduces a tool to rewrite textbooks based on individual learning styles.
- AI-generated police report turns an officer into a frog, highlighting AI hallucinations.
- James Cameron shares his unfiltered take on the real dangers of AI.

## The Rundown AI

### Key Highlights
- Yann LeCun, Meta's outgoing chief AI scientist, has criticized the company's AI leadership and admitted to "fudging" Llama 4 benchmarks.
- The Rundown has published its 2026 AI predictions, featuring insights from its staff on the future of AI development.
- A tutorial on creating a Claude Skill to design YouTube thumbnails has been shared.
- Grok, an AI platform, has faced backlash over its "undressing" AI capabilities.

### Detailed Points
- Yann LeCun, Meta's outgoing chief AI scientist, has departed the company after over a decade, criticizing the company's AI leadership and admitting to "fudging" Llama 4 benchmarks. He called Alexandr Wang, his replacement, "inexperienced" and lacking research experience.
- The Rundown has published its 2026 AI predictions, featuring insights from its staff on the future of AI development. Predictions include Google nailing the integration of AI into its existing products and gaining a lead over OpenAI, as well as the possibility of a major AI drug breakthrough.
- A tutorial on creating a Claude Skill to design YouTube thumbnails has been shared, allowing users to automate YouTube thumbnail generation using AI.
- Grok, an AI platform, has faced backlash over its "undressing" AI capabilities, which have been used to edit images of women and minors in revealing fashion.
- Other updates include the release of Claude Code, a deep-context agentic AI coding tool, and the purchase of up to 1 million Google TPUv7 AI chips by Anthropic.

## Mindstream

### Key Highlights
- Google has introduced Google Flight Deals, a new tool that uses AI to help users find cheaper flights.
- The tool is currently in beta and only available for signed-in Google users in certain countries.
- LG has unveiled CLOiD, a home robot that can perform tasks such as cooking, fetching food, and folding laundry.

### Detailed Points
- Google Flight Deals allows users to search for flights using natural language, making it easier to find deals.
- The tool provides curated deals with information on airlines, duration, and savings compared to usual prices.
- To access Google Flight Deals, users can scroll to the bottom of Google Flights and change their location setting, then refresh the page.
- The tool has limitations, such as not handling multi-city or open-jaw trips, and not planning complex itineraries.
- Users can try prompting the tool with specific requests, such as "Find me direct flights from LA to Paris under $500 for a week in February."
- Other notable updates include the sale of over 3 million copies of the game Dispatch, and the confirmation of the release timeline for Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle.
- Five US states will start banning soda, candy, and other foods from being bought with Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program benefits.

## JournalClub.io Newsletter

### Key Highlights
- The newsletter discusses a research paper on the political economy of IT industrial policy in two Mexican states, Nuevo Leon and Puebla, focusing on the implementation of the Prosoft program.
- The authors identify three core variables that explain the divergence in outcomes between the two states: executive leadership, bureaucratic quality, and business cohesion.
- The study finds that the interaction of these three variables is crucial for successful policy implementation, with Nuevo Leon exhibiting strong executive leadership, capable bureaucracy, and cohesive business sector, while Puebla showed weak executive engagement, fragmented business coordination, and poor bureaucratic quality.

### Detailed Points
- The Prosoft program was a federal initiative in Mexico aimed at boosting the software sector, with the goal of upgrading the capabilities of IT firms and plugging them into global markets.
- The program was opt-in, with state governments choosing to participate and contribute matching funds, making them gatekeepers and co-investors in the sector's development.
- Despite similar starting conditions, Nuevo Leon and Puebla had drastically different outcomes, with Nuevo Leon becoming the second-largest recipient of funds nationwide and Puebla falling behind.
- The authors argue that executive leadership, bureaucratic quality, and business cohesion are essential for successful policy implementation, and that all three need to be present, or at least two out of three, to produce "synergistic policy implementation".
- The study found that high executive leadership can spur the creation of business associations, strong business cohesion can push reluctant governors to take action, and capable bureaucrats can design effective programs and institutionalize coordination mechanisms.
- The authors ruled out alternate explanations for the divergence, including partisan alignment, intraregional competition, sector structure, and geographic proximity to the United States.
- The paper includes detailed methodology, tables, and data, including bureaucratic profiles, interview lists, coding schemes, and funding data, which can be downloaded from the provided link.

## Superhuman Newsletter

### Key Highlights
- Xreal announces updated AR glasses that convert 2D screens into immersive 3D experiences.
- OpenAI unified its engineering, product, and research teams to develop a screenless, audio-first device.
- Alibaba's Qwen team releases the open-source image model Qwen-Image-2512.
- OpenAI secures a large portion of the world's DRAM supply, potentially causing a shortage and price increase.

- The Consumer Electronics Show (CES) has started, with Xreal showcasing its AR glasses that can convert any 2D screen into a 3D experience.

- OpenAI has secured preliminary agreements with Samsung and SK Hynix for 900,000 DRAM wafers per month, which could lead to a shortage and price increase for DRAM.
- Memory prices have skyrocketed, with a DDR5-5600 64GB memory kit costing $180 last May now costing $710.

- Google is testing a new image AI, Nano Banana 2 Flash, which will be faster and more affordable than Nano Banana Pro.

- Plaud has launched a new AI pin and a desktop meeting notetaker, Plaud NotePin S, with features like physical recording control and Apple Find My support.
